label: copy-phase input r (fed-back r) in short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases), on steps whose input is the fed-back token r, i.e. the step right after the model has output r. 99.7% of activation mass is on in_tok == r. It is length-dependent: firing rate falls off sharply for L >= 7 (L 7-9 hold under 5% of mass). The largest activations (about 6) are in L=3 sequences where r is the first original token and is fed back at the first copy step, e.g. r p q <DEL> [r] p. Activations get weaker with longer sequences. It does not fire on r during the original phase (in_first == 1 never fires) or on other input tokens, apart from a small residue of low activations (0.3% of mass) on other inputs at the first copy step of short sequences.

issues: The remaining errors come from the gradual drop with length, not from a hidden variable. At L=6, r inputs in the copy phase fire with precision 0.61. At L=7 it is 0.18, and at L<=5 it is 0.98. Splitting L=6 by digit count, in_count or recall_idx (precision 0.56-0.68) does not separate firing from non-firing steps, so the cutoff at L<=6 is a magnitude threshold on a graded signal.
None of the other cutoffs beat L<=6. t<=9 gave F1 0.74, t<=10 gave 0.70, 2L+recall_idx<=15 gave 0.79, L<=5 gave 0.72 (precision 0.98, recall 0.57) and to_go/recall_idx combinations gave 0.59-0.77.

The secondary claims check out. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Copy-phase inputs other than r hold 0.26% of the mass, almost all at L=3 on the first copy step. The top activations (about 6.2) are L=3 sequences that start with r, with r fed back at the first copy step. An r at L=3 on the first copy step fires every time (precision 1.0).

Test misses are steps with r at L=7-8 and small activations. Test false positives are r inputs late in L=6 sequences and second r's in a repeat. Both fit the length falloff, and missed activations hold only 4.6% of the mass.

The label is a little loose: 'short sequences' really means a strength that falls off steadily with L, with L=6 already around 60% precision. That is acceptable, but the explanation should say the feature weakens gradually rather than stopping at a cutoff.
Reproduced test scores: precision 0.826, recall 0.825, F1 0.825, mass recall 0.954.
